A here-string that writes before anyone is reading

tests/evals/test-dead-generation-guard.sh, #3190 · bash 5.3 backs <<< with a pipe and writes the payload before the reader exists · past the pipe capacity the write blocks forever · 2026-09-11

The mechanism, in one sentence

grep -q PAT <<< "$BODY"     bash forks NOTHING for the payload
                            it opens a pipe, writes $BODY itself,
                            THEN spawns the reader
                            payload > pipe capacity: the write blocks,
                            nobody is draining, forever, at 0% CPU

printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep PAT
                            producer and consumer exist at the same time,
                            the kernel buffer always drains, every size

Recorded evidence: the same binary, Homebrew bash 5.3.15, hung 6/6 on 2026-07-29 with payloads from 512 B up, and passed 48/48 trials on 2026-08-13. The 512 B cutover matches PIPE_BUF, the atomic-write floor, while macOS pipes hold 16 KB and grow to 64 KB. The fits: under fd or memory pressure the kernel declines to grow the pipe past its floor. The capacity that gates the deadlock is environment-dependent.

What the fix changed, exactly two lines

     if grep -q "classify_generation" <<< "$BODY"printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep "classify_generation" > /dev/null; then
     if grep -q "for attempt in 1 2" <<< "$BODY"printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep "for attempt in 1 2" > /dev/null; then

Why no -q on the pipe: this suite runs set -uo pipefail. grep -q exits on the first match and SIGPIPEs the producer, which under pipefail races 141 into the if and flips a pass to a fail (#603). Without -q the consumer drains stdin to EOF and the exit status is the same.

Local verification: bash tests/evals/test-dead-generation-guard.sh on macOS: Passed: 14, Failed: 0, six of six runs, under bash 5.3.15 and bash 3.2.57.
